pairs.why: The two kettles are almost identical: the same glossy red enamel, chrome knob and soft purple light, so neither is closer to the real cards.
The kettles match in shape, gloss and lighting, and the small difference in background gradient doesn't make either one closer.
B has fewer, larger and smoother vegetable slices with less busy detail, closer to the clean, readable chunks on the real fruit plate.
A's larger, simpler tomato and carrot slices read cleaner and less fussy, closer to the real cards, while B packs in more small pieces.
A's chunkier handle and slightly thicker wires give it the stylized proportions of the real cards; B is thinner and more realistic.
A's handle is fuller and rounder, so it reads like a stylized game prop, while B's slimmer build leans realistic.
A's faucet is slightly thicker and chunkier with bolder water drops, a little closer to the stylized props, though the two are nearly the same.
A's spout and body are slightly heavier and rounder, a little closer to the real cards' chunky stylization, but the difference is small.
